Thanks, Emma — helpful notes. Short clarifications from our side: 

- Onshore fallback / caching: Redwood's inference runtime keeps a KV cache to accelerate recurrent tokens. By default the cache resides on the serving node in-region; for EU customers the primary cache remains in region. We do have an optional onshore fallback feature that routes inference to an onshore pool (UK-only) when regional capacity is constrained — that would be called out in the IDTA and requires explicit opt-in. Retention for cache metadata is 24 hours by default; we can shorten to 12 hours for regulated clients.

- Evidence types we typically collect for TIAs/DTIAs: architecture diagram (PNG/PDF), access logs (CSV, redacted), subprocessor list (CSV), encryption-at-rest key management statements (PDF), and pseudonymization approach (short narrative + code pointers if applicable).

I uploaded a sample mapping template and a short evidence checklist to the Drive link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aBcD-evidence-pack — please drop a single consolidated list of required artifacts there by EOD Wed and we’ll queue Kimberly to assemble the pack.

Also: if MedSync legal wants a short demo of the runtime routing (to validate residency guarantees), we can do a 30-min technical walkthrough this week.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
